originalTitle: Stanford bilim insanları Alzheimer'ı semptomlardan yıllar önce tahmin eden gizli beyin sinyalleri keşfetti
titleEn: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
headline: Stanford bilim insanları Alzheimer'ı semptomlardan yıllar önce tahmin eden gizli beyin sinyalleri keşfetti.
details: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers.
brief: Subtle patterns of brain activity may reveal the risk of Alzheimer's disease years before memory problems develop or harmful proteins begin accumulating in the brain, according to new research led by Stanford Medicine.
summary: Subtle patterns of brain activity may reveal the risk of Alzheimer's disease years before memory problems develop or harmful proteins begin accumulating in the brain, according to new research led by Stanford Medicine. The same approach can also identify people whose brains show exceptional resistance to cognitive decline, suggesting they may eventually become "super agers. " The study, published November 4 in Science Advances , points to a potentially powerful new way to detect early warning signs of cognitive decline. Unlike conventional biomarkers, these patterns of brain activity might eventually be possible to change through targeted interventions.
